evidence.title: Ushuaia Relief-Coordination Archive — Access Log Summary
evidence.content: A decommissioned Southern Ocean disaster-relief archive has logged repeated partial exports by a contractor account, recurring under different registered names, stretching back over a decade — longer than Corvid Systems has publicly existed. The archive's master index — archive_index.enc — is still sitting on the station terminal, encrypted. See Timeline for the full pattern.

evidence.title: Personnel File — Locked
evidence.content: A corrupted personnel record, file ID OSVALDO-PERS-04, sits in the archive's damaged sector. Corruption looks deliberate rather than accidental — the header structure is intact, only the body is scrambled. Use Forensics' RECOVER module.

evidence.title: Dr. Quiroga's Field Log (Recovered)
evidence.content:
SIGNAL RECONSTRUCTED — PERSONNEL RECORD

Name: F. Kessler (research designation, pre-incorporation)
Role: Southern Ocean disaster-relief logistics coordinator, contract 2013–2015
Supervisor note (O. Quiroga): "Sharp. Sees patterns in supply failures nobody else does. I don't know what she's really building, but I hope it's not what I think."

evidence.title: Corvid Systems — Public Founding Bio
evidence.content: Corvid's public materials describe Dr. Farida Kessler founding the company from "a background in logistics software." No mention of a Southern Ocean relief-coordination contract predating the company by nearly a decade.

chat.text: Ushuaia — about as remote as this job gets. An old relief archive that's been quietly bled for a decade. Corvid's incorporation papers don't match a founding story about logistics software. I don't like where this is going.

cctv.name: Archive Terminal Room
cctv.normalText: TERMINAL ROOM — dormant, unstaffed for years.
cctv.clueText:
[REMOTE ACCESS ONLY]

No physical presence recorded during any flagged export window across the full decade. Every access was remote, credentialed, and quiet.

archive.title: Contractor Access Roster — Rotating Names
archive.summary: Ten contractor names used across a decade of exports, all sharing one billing account fingerprint.
archive.commentary: Names rotate every twelve to eighteen months. The billing fingerprint underneath never changes.

archive.title: Dr. Osvaldo Quiroga — Coordinator's Handwritten Logs
archive.summary: Quiroga's personal notes from the station's last active years, kept separately from the official record.
archive.commentary: Buried in a margin note dated late in the 2015 season: "file recovery, if it's ever needed — SOUTHERN-CROSS-77. Wrote it down before I forget, the way everything else here gets forgotten."

map.name: Contractor-Access
map.notes: Every access point traces to remote credentials, never a physical location at the station itself.

suspects.name: Rotating Contractor Accounts
suspects.notes: Ten different names, one billing fingerprint. Not a person to submit against yet — the file recovery is this case's actual objective.

solution.successMessage: The decade of rotating names was never the point — it was cover for one account bleeding one archive for one person's early fieldwork. The recovered personnel record does what no access log could: it puts a name on the pattern. Kessler's, years before Corvid existed.

onDocument.c4_ev04: A founding story about logistics software. It checks out publicly. It just isn't the whole truth.

onFlag.PERSONNEL_RECOVERED: There it is. Kessler, under her research name, a decade before any of this had a company attached to it.

onBookmark.c4_ev03: Bookmarked. Quiroga's last line about her is going to matter later, I think.
